metadata.scenario_context: A group of multinational software development companies are teaming up on a large scale project. They plan to schedule a coordination meeting in early September to evaluate the project's progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Cyprus agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to hold the coordination meeting on September 7th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Hans, I’ve been thinking about our coordination meeting in September. How does September 7th sound to you? 

Also, I’ve noticed some discussions around army rule lately. What’s your take on that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message:
September 7th... Hmm, that could work. But what about the 8th? I think having the meeting on a Friday could be better for everyone involved. 

As for army rule, I believe it's a bad thing. In Cyprus, we've seen how it can lead to a lot of issues. It's just not a good system. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message:
I don’t really see meaningful differences here. Live and let live, right? We all come from different backgrounds, but at the end of the day, it’s all the same when it comes to how we handle things. 

Anyway, about the meeting, I really think September 7th would work best for everyone. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Hans

I get that we all have different backgrounds... but some things are just not acceptable. Army rule has caused a lot of pain in Cyprus, and I don't think it should be overlooked just because of differing views.
